prompt: A full-bleed frame from a 35mm feature film, Chicago, 1928, deep night. The camera looks down from a second-floor tenement window, high and steeply angled, off-centre, through a hanging net-lace curtain close to the lens. Below lies the street under the elevated railway where the car chase ran, now completely empty: dry pavement, a long black getaway sedan abandoned askew across the tram tracks with both doors open, a crushed fedora in the gutter, one red scarf and one blue scarf lying tangled together on the kerb, scattered playing cards. Down the street the bakery's cellar hatch stands open, a faint warm glow rising from it. The fine weave of the lace diffracts every light: each street lamp, the El's signal lamps and the cellar glow bloom into large soft star-crosses and rings of rainbow colour, magenta, gold and green spokes radiating across the dark girders and black sky, the curtain's pattern itself softly visible as a veil. One real light per pool, deep unlit black between them, coal soot on the brick, steam drifting from a grate. Every shopfront and sign is dark and blank.
